newsitem.title: SPAIN: Gun shots sprayed across Basque police barracks.
newsitem.headline: Gun shots sprayed across Basque police barracks.

text.p: Gun shots were fired at a civil guard barracks in the northern Basque city of San Sebastian in the early hours of Sunday in what police believe was an attack by the separatist group ETA.
Police said no one was hurt.
The shots were fired from a stolen taxi at the barracks in the old quarter of the city. One officer was standing guard at the time of the attack but was unhurt, police said.
"This was probably an attack by ETA but we cannot confirm that right now," a police spokeswoman said.
The attack came just hours after around 100 hooded youths clashed with police in the city during the traditionally heated fiesta season.
Youths threw fireworks and stones at police and launched petrol bombs at a bus and a church. Police said no one was injured.
Following the attack on the barracks, police located eight bullet marks on the front of the building and a casing from a 9-mm weapon, the sort commonly used by the ETA, the civil guard said.
Police found the taxi which had been stolen by two men, abandoned in the city.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people in a 29-year violent campaign for an independent Basque state.
